key_insight: Increasing plunge depth improves simulated interface heating and material flow in AA6061–SS304 friction stir lap welding while leaving peak workpiece temperature nearly unchanged.
engineering_relevance: The study identifies 0.15–0.30 mm as a promising plunge-depth range for balancing interfacial bonding conditions and welding stability.
method: Finite-volume computational fluid dynamics model of dissimilar friction stir lap welding.
Plunge depth varied from 0 to 0.45 mm.
Fixed rotation at 1200 rpm, traverse speed at 100 mm/min, and tool tilt at 1.5°.
evidence_signal: Across the simulated range, peak interface temperature rose from 743 to 791 K and velocity from 0.07865 to 0.08121 m/s, while minimum interface viscosity fell by approximately 23.7% and tool torque by 7%.
watch_item: The abstract reports simulation results but no experimental validation or joint-strength measurements, so bonding improvements and the proposed depth range require verification.
paper_title: Thermal-mechanical response to plunge depth variation in friction stir lap welding of AA6061 and SS304-computational fluid dynamics approach
